source: Indian Railways PRS static page 'Tatkal Scheme' (CRIS), https://www.indianrail.gov.in/tatkal_Scheme.html, table 'Tatkal Charges applicable for journey starting from 24.12.2015 onwards' and the header rule 'The Tatkal Charges have been fixed as a percentage of fare at the rate of 10% of basic fare for second class and 30% of basic fare for all other classes subject to minimum and maximum as given in the table below.' Page fetched and text-extracted 2026-10-29 (32818 bytes); the same table is published on IRCTC's Tatkal FAQ page, contents.irctc.co.in/en/TatkalFaq.html.
season_note: The page settles it in one sentence: 'The above charges will be levied uniformly both in peak period & non-peak periods.' There is no peak or lean Tatkal band to model.
not_in_scheme_note: 1A: the scheme prints no AC First Class row, and IRCTC's terms say a Tatkal ticket may be booked in 'any class except 1 AC'. FC: the page prints no First Class row either, so no charge can be quoted for it rather than an invented one.
inherit_note: 3E is not printed as its own row. Its basic fare is the 3A table's, so the 3A band is used and the quote says so.
min_km_note: The page heads this column 'Minimum Distance for charge (in Km)'. It is carried as printed and is not multiplied into the charge: the printed floor in rupees is what makes the published fare come out right at short distances (CC at 192 km is 30% of basic = 86.40, and the published Tatkal fare is built on the 125 rupee floor).

timings.advance_rule: Tatkal booking opens at 10 AM for AC Classes and 11 AM for NON-AC Classes one day in advance of the actual date of journey, excluding the date of journey (Railway Board commercial circular 34 of 2015, w.e.f. 15.06.2015).
